## Problem
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:196` and
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:413` hardcode a `severity` string
(`"critical"`, `"high"`) directly into a kernel-shaped finding without ever running through
`pass3_decide` (`review_kernel/decide.py`), so these DET-tier findings carry no computed
`validity`/`impact`/`priority`. The epic is migrating every consumer of `severity`
(aggregation ranking, the review-bot comment, the `fail_on_severity` workflow gate) onto
`priority` instead; DET-tier findings need a `priority` value before those consumers can
treat all findings uniformly. Both sites already carry `"decision": "block"` alongside
`severity` -- only the `severity` key itself needs replacing.

## Approach
At each hardcode site, replace the `severity` key with a fixed `priority` float, keeping the
existing `"decision": "block"` key and always-block semantics unchanged: the secrets
detector's finding always blocks, so its priority is pinned above every configured
`block_threshold` (`priority: 1.0`); the bugfix-size-gate's finding is a
strong-but-not-maximal signal (`priority: 0.9`). No new key is introduced -- `decision` is
already present at both sites; this task only swaps `severity` for `priority`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `detectors.py`'s secrets-detector finding carries `priority: 1.0` (and its existing
  `decision: "block"` is unchanged) instead of `severity: "critical"`.
- [ ] `bugfix_size_gate.py`'s size-gate finding carries `priority: 0.9` (and its existing
  `decision: "block"` is unchanged) instead of `severity: "high"`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py -k failclosed_match_names_blocking` and
  `pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py -k test_oversized_bug_fix_without_attestation_blocks`
  pass, with assertions on the new `priority` key (`test_code_review_ws5.py:196` currently
  asserts `entry["severity"] == "critical"`; `test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:240-243` currently
  has no severity/priority assertion at all).
- [ ] `grep -rn '"severity"' src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`
  returns no matches.

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit test against the real detector/gate functions (pure calculation, no
I/O). Oracle: the returned finding dict's `priority` value, asserted exactly (`decision` is
already covered by existing assertions and is unchanged). Existing tests
`test_code_review_ws5.py::test_...` (line ~196) and
`test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py::test_oversized_bug_fix_without_attestation_blocks` (line
~240) are the RED oracles to strengthen.
